prompt.context: Lion King Bank is a consumer bank in South Africa providing checking, savings, credit cards, loans, etc. They have branches in all 9 South African provinces. They have completed an aggressive cost-cutting program, but revenues are still low and profitability is also low. They are looking to fix this and improve profitability quickly, and they've come to us to help them find a solution.
prompt.question: The company is looking to dramatically increase revenues in 2 years. How would you approach improving Lion King Bank's profitability?

clarifying_info.q: Has anything changed in the competitive landscape recently?
clarifying_info.a: Nothing has changed about the competitive landscape recently.

exhibits.title: Student Market Sizing Data
exhibits.shows: A table with rows for Youth population, % students, % using banking, and LKB share, with columns for Current (Year 1) and Year 3 projected values, plus CAGR. The Year 3 column is partially blank — the candidate must calculate the projected figures.

framework: Revenues: decompose as Number of accounts × money earned per account (fees / spread between saving and borrowing rates)
Customers: identify segments (demographics, growth opportunities, revenue potential / LTV, acquisition & retention, premium segments)
Product Mix: evaluate existing product mix vs potential expansion opportunities
Competition: benchmark fees and product offerings against competitors

questions.prompt: The company is looking to dramatically increase revenues in 2 years. What ideas do you have on how to do this?
questions.guidance: A strong answer recognizes that costs have already been cut, so the lever is revenue. Key drivers are (1) increasing number of customer accounts and (2) increasing money earned per existing account. Candidate should cover: capturing unbanked customers, acquiring customers from competitors (via better product mix or lower fees), selling more products to existing customers, increasing rates, and evaluating expansion into alternative markets or geographies.

questions.prompt: There are two customer segments they are evaluating: students and affluent middle-class customers. They already have many mid-income customers and are looking at expanding student customers. How would you evaluate the student market and how might you target students?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose a market-sizing structure (top-down: population → % students → % banked → LKB share). After they articulate an approach, show Exhibit 1. Strong answers calculate projected Year 3 accounts and identify this as a high-growth segment. Ways to reach students: campus branding and tie-ups, branches near campuses, student-friendly products (student loans, low/no fee accounts, low balance requirements), and targeting parents who already have accounts.

math.setup: Starting from youth population of 5,000,000 growing at 10% CAGR, % students doubling (100% CAGR effectively means the student share moves from 10% to 20%), % using banking rising from 50% to 75%, and LKB share rising from 10% to 20%.
steps: Year 3 youth population = 5,000,000 × (1.10)^3 ≈ 6,050,000 (using ~3-year horizon, simplified as 5M × 1.21 ≈ 6,050,000)
math.answer: LKB student accounts grow from ~25,000 to ~181,500, roughly a 7x increase — a highly attractive growth opportunity if LKB can maintain or grow its market share.

questions.prompt: The company does some research and finds that students can only be acquired through heavy price discounts. Should the company focus on student accounts or affluent mid-income accounts?
questions.guidance: Key insight: student accounts have very high growth potential in number and high lifetime value, but will NOT translate into near-term revenue growth because LKB cannot earn significant fees from students (heavy discounts required). Since the firm needs to improve revenues immediately (within 2 years), the correct recommendation is to prioritize affluent mid-income customers now. Tactics for mid-income customers: improve product range (e.g. mutual funds, fixed income accounts), improve product attractiveness (lower fees, better rates), push more products to existing customers, and improve ease of access (branch network, digital channels).

brainstorming.prompt: How would you target and acquire affluent mid-income customers?

categories.name: Product improvements
ideas: Add mutual fund and fixed income account offerings
Lower fees and improve interest rates to be more competitive
Bundle products (e.g. checking + savings + credit card packages)

categories.name: Sales and marketing
ideas: Referral programs from existing mid-income customers
Targeted digital and social media advertising

categories.name: Distribution and access
ideas: Evaluate branch network coverage and add locations in underserved areas
Partner with employers for payroll banking

categories.name: Retention
ideas: Dedicated relationship managers for high-value accounts
Improve customer service and complaint resolution

recommendation: Lion King Bank should prioritize the affluent mid-income customer segment in the short term to drive the rapid revenue increase the company needs within 2 years

While student accounts offer strong long-term lifetime value and a ~7x growth opportunity in account numbers, they require heavy price discounts and will not generate meaningful fee revenue in the near term

LKB should target mid-income customers by improving its product range, offering competitive fees and rates, pushing additional products to its existing customer base, and improving geographic and digital access
risks: Aggressively acquiring mid-income customers from competitors may trigger price wars on fees and rates, compressing margins
Ignoring the student segment entirely risks losing future profitable customers given high switching costs later in life
Expanding product range (e.g. mutual funds) requires regulatory approval and operational capability
next_steps: Conduct in-depth analysis of the current product mix to identify optimization opportunities and gaps vs competitors
Develop a phased plan to eventually convert student account holders into profitable full-service customers
Identify new revenue sources through potential geographic expansion into underserved provinces
